label: Customers
name: customers
description: A registry of customers: the routes talk to a REST API (mockapi.io); customers are imported from and exported to CSV files through the blob registry. Customers are kept per tenant, the tenant the sign-in wrote into the caller's session; reads are for a signed-in caller, and writes for signed-in employees holding the registrar role, identified by our own token, issued by the included access tree (@wilanis/access) at /api/v1/auth-employees against a directory this project binds (account holders sign in at /api/v1/auth-customers and hold a token too, and read their own tenant's customers, but no write). Preferences live in the session. A command-line greeting is gated by a one-time code. Plugins come from npm packages named by "from".

otp.description: a one-time code: printed by the issue-otp command in this example, delivered out of band in a real tree -- the binding of access.port.json#deliverCode decides

includes.description: sign-in, sessions, policies and the one-time code, as a tree of their own; identity.port.json is bound below, in features/directories

startup.label: Prepare the customer store
startup.description: Make storage ready once, before anything reads it: under local that creates the collections the store declares, and under live there is nothing to create, so it reads the collection once. Only a startup step prepares, and only because project.json says so.

startup.label: Make the customers whole
startup.description: Repair every record the storage holds that predates what a customer means here: one read, then one write per record that carries no address or no tier, paced by the connection. It runs before the port opens, so no route ever answers a record this tree cannot vouch for, and it writes nothing on a second run. Under a store there is nothing to repair and the step passes over every record untouched.

startup.label: Reach the customer store
startup.description: Read the customers once before the HTTP server opens, so a tree whose storage is unreachable refuses to serve instead of answering every route with a fault. It reads every tenant's, since nobody is calling yet and a startup step has no tenant to read (B008). The port is bound per profile, so this checks whatever storage the profile chose.

startup.label: Prepare the guard's memory
startup.description: Create the collections auth.store.json declares, once, before anything reads them. It runs under production and production-scheduler, where the guard's sessions and challenges are records in the database every instance shares, and whichever process starts first creates them; the laptop's profiles keep one file per record and have nothing to create.

startup.label: Reach the guard's memory
startup.description: Read one session through @auth/state.port.json before the HTTP server opens, so a tree whose sessions and challenges cannot be reached refuses to serve rather than refusing every signed-in caller. No session is kept under this key, so a reachable store answers nothing; the profile's binding decides which store that is.

startup.label: Watch for changes
startup.description: Serve the tree again whenever a document changes, without closing the port. A change that does not pass wilanis check is reported and the last good tree keeps answering. It runs on the laptop, under live and local; production serves the documents it started with, and a new version is a new process.

startup.label: Keep the schedule
startup.description: Fire the scheduled triggers of this tree, each at the instants its cron expression names. This tree declares none: its customers are kept per tenant, and a tick has no caller to be a tenant of, so a scheduled trigger could reach neither them nor the view across them. Delete this step and nothing is scheduled: a scheduled trigger fires because project.json asks for a scheduler, never because the trigger exists. It runs on the laptop, under live and local, where one process is the only one there is, so it holds nothing.

startup.label: Keep the schedule in one process
startup.description: The same scheduler, run by the one process started under production-scheduler, while the instances behind the load balancer run production and only listen: one process schedules, so a tick is fired once however many instances serve the routes. Each tick is still held in the customer database, which declares leases, so the moment a rolling deploy runs an old scheduler beside its replacement, whichever reaches a tick first fires it and the other finds it taken.

startup.label: Export traces
startup.description: Send every run this tree serves to an OpenTelemetry collector at localhost:4318, as spans. Delete this step and nothing is exported: traces leave the process because project.json says so, never because the runtime decided a tree should phone home. It is not required, because no collector is running when you clone this example: the step only subscribes, so it succeeds with nothing listening, and every batch it then cannot send is said once in the log and dropped rather than delaying or failing the run whose trace it was. Run `wilanis run <trigger> example --trace` to read the same spans on your terminal with no collector at all.

startup.label: Listen
startup.description: Open the HTTP port and answer this tree's routes. Delete this step and nothing listens: a tree serves because it says so, never because a trigger exists. It runs under every profile but production-scheduler, the process that keeps the schedule and serves no route.

live.description: The laptop, and the default, so `npx wilanis start example` names no profile: the customers through their REST API, the directories written in the connections, and a reload on every saved document.

local.description: Everything in this process: the customers kept in memory, the directories written in the connections, and a reload on every saved document. Nothing reaches the network, so `wilanis start example --profile local` serves the same routes with no upstream at all.

production.description: Behind the load balancer, started with `wilanis start example --profile production`: the customers in PostgreSQL, the one operator account in place of the laptop's employees, and nothing watched. The same routes, policies, shapes and business graphs as every other profile, and not one document under features/ changes: another binding meets customer.port.json, and every reference to employees.connection.json reaches employees-production.connection.json instead. The startup steps prepare the database before the port opens, so a tree whose database is unreachable refuses to serve rather than answering every route with a fault. It listens and keeps no schedule: run as many of it as the load needs, and one process under production-scheduler beside them.

production-scheduler.description: The one process that keeps the schedule beside production, started with `wilanis start example --profile production-scheduler`: production's bindings and connections, so a tick reaches what a route there reaches, and production's startup but for the listener, which it never opens. Run one of it and as many production instances as the load needs; those listen and schedule nothing.
